newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says takes back western area from rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says takes back western area from rebels.

text.p: The Sudanese army has recaptured an area in western Sudan from Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) guerrillas, state media said on Sunday.

The government-owned al-Anbaa daily said the army along with the volunteer Popular Defence Force had "achieved a big victory in Western Kordofan by liberating all of Jebel Taleshi and the areas of Ras el-Fil, Dordi, Saada, Salgaya, Shada and Lambo".
The paper said the military operation started on May 25 and ended on May 31.

"After the achievement of this victory, the road linking Lagawa to Deling (in neighbouring Southern Kordofan state) has been opened," the paper quoted Western Kordofan governor Hassan Osman Rizig as saying.
Al-Anbaa said government forces lost "three martyrs" but did not give casualties for the rebels. State television said the SPLA suffered "huge losses" but did not elaborate.
Government troops set free 500 people who were being held prisoner by the rebels, the paper said.
Rebels had used Jebel Taleshi, a mountainous area, as a strategic centre from which they launched many anti-government operations, al-Anbaa said.

The SPLA has fought since 1983 for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north. It has recently allied itself with Moslem rebels under an umbrella coalition that aims to trigger an uprising in Khartoum.
